Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels

Source: R/modelterms.R
modelterms.Rd

A standalone, zero-dependency suite of functions to seamlessly manipulate terms objects, formulas, fitted models, and character vectors of term labels.

Usage

as_terms(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  intercept = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  keep.order = NULL,
  env = parent.frame(),
  ...
)

has_intercept(x, ...)

has_response(x, ...)

get_response(x, raw = FALSE, ...)

get_order(x, ...)

get_labels(x, ...)

get_variables(x, raw = FALSE, each.term = FALSE, ...)

filter_terms(
  x,
  keep = NULL,
  drop = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  require = NULL,
  remove = NULL,
  raw = TRUE,
  response = TRUE,
  intercept = TRUE,
  ...
)

is_single_term(x, ...)

is_fully_crossed(x, ...)

make_signature(x, strict = TRUE, ...)

match_labels(x, y, strict = TRUE, nomatch = c("pass", "omit", "fail"), ...)

Arguments

x, y

an object representing model terms: a terms object, a formula, a fitted model object, or a character vector. In as_terms(), y specifies an optional response variable (as a character string or language object). In match_labels(), y is the target object whose term labels are matched against.

intercept

logical. In as_terms(), should an intercept be included by default when coercing a character vector? Defaults to FALSE. Explicit tokens in x (such as "1" or "+1") override this default. In filter_terms(), whether to retain the intercept of x.

data

a data.frame used to resolve . in formulas or shorthand strings.

keep.order

logical. Should terms be kept in their input order rather than sorted by interaction order? Defaults to TRUE for strict term label vectors and FALSE for formulas or length-1 formula shorthands.

env

an environment to attach to the resulting terms object when coercing from a character vector. Defaults to parent.frame().

...

additional arguments passed to terms or as_terms().

raw

logical. If FALSE (default in get_variables() and get_response()), returns model expressions (e.g., "log(x2)"). If TRUE (default in filter_terms()), extracts or filters by underlying raw column names (e.g., "x2").

each.term

logical. If FALSE (default), get_variables() returns a flat character vector across the whole model. If TRUE, returns a named list mapping each term label to its constituent variables.

keep, drop

a character vector of term labels (matched order-invariantly via match_labels()) or an integer vector of term indices to explicitly retain (keep) or exclude (drop) in filter_terms().

order

an integer vector specifying interaction orders to retain in filter_terms() (e.g., 1L for main effects, 2L for two-way interactions).

require

a character vector of variable names. Only terms containing at least one of these variables are retained.

remove

a character vector of variable names. Any terms containing these variables are excluded.

response

logical. Whether to retain the response variable in filter_terms(). Defaults to TRUE.

strict

logical. If TRUE (default), make_signature() and match_labels() require each element to be a single valid term.

nomatch

character string specifying how to handle unmatched labels in match_labels(): "pass" (returns NA), "omit" (drops unmatched elements), or "fail" (throws an error).

Value

  • as_terms(), filter_terms(): a terms object.

  • has_intercept(), has_response(), is_single_term(), is_fully_crossed(): a scalar logical (TRUE or FALSE).

  • get_order(): a named integer vector of term orders.

  • get_labels(), make_signature(), match_labels(): a character vector.

  • get_response(): a character string (when raw = FALSE), a character vector of variable names (when raw = TRUE), or NULL if no response exists.

  • get_variables(): a character vector (when each.term = FALSE) or a named list of character vectors (when each.term = TRUE).

Details

Three Levels of Model Components

For a model formula such as y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2), this package distinguishes three structural levels:

  1. Term Labels (get_labels(x)): The individual additive components of the model: c("x1", "log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)", "x1:log(x2)").

  2. Model Variables (get_variables(x, raw = FALSE)): The distinct predictor expressions forming the terms (rows of the "factors" matrix): c("x1", "log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)").

  3. Raw Variables (get_variables(x, raw = TRUE)): The underlying column names required in data: c("x1", "x2").

Character Input Rules in as_terms()

When x is a character vector, as_terms() distinguishes between a vector of strict term labels and a length-1 formula shorthand:

  • Strict Term Labels (character(n)): If every element (excluding intercept tokens like "1" or "-1") represents strictly a single valid term (e.g., c("b:a", "a", "I(x^2)")), input order and exact interaction notation ("b:a") are preserved by default (keep.order = TRUE).

  • Length-1 Formula Shorthand (character(1)): If x is a single string containing formula operators or . (e.g., ".^2", ".", or "a * b + c + 1"), it is expanded as a right-hand side formula expression (using data if needed) and sorted by interaction order by default (keep.order = FALSE).

  • Invalid Mixed Vectors (length(x) >= 2): If x has length 2 or more and contains any non-single-term expression (such as c("a * b", "c") or c(".", "a")), an informative error is thrown.

Safe Alternatives to Base R stats Functions

filter_terms() serves as a declarative, crash-safe replacement for drop.terms, delete.response, and [.terms:

  • filter_terms(x, response = FALSE) safely removes the response variable like stats::delete.response(x).

  • filter_terms(x, drop = ...) and filter_terms(x, keep = ...) subset specific terms by character label (order-invariant) or numeric index without crashing when all terms are dropped.

Examples

# Coercion with as_terms()
t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1"))
get_labels(t1)
#> [1] "b:a" "a"  
has_intercept(t1)
#> [1] TRUE

t2 <- as_terms(".^2", y = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4])
get_labels(t2)
#> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp"
#> [6] "Wind:Temp"   

# Extracting labels, variables, and response at three levels
fml <- log(y) ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
get_response(fml, raw = FALSE)
#> [1] "log(y)"
get_response(fml, raw = TRUE)
#> [1] "y"
get_labels(fml)
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" "x1:log(x2)"
get_variables(fml, raw = FALSE)
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE)
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE, each.term = TRUE)
#> $x1
#> [1] "x1"
#> 
#> $`log(x2)`
#> [1] "x2"
#> 
#> $`I(x1 * x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
#> 
#> $`x1:log(x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
#> 

# Filtering terms by order, variables, or specific term labels
fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels()
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
fml |> filter_terms(require = "x2", remove = "x1", raw = TRUE) |> get_labels()
#> [1] "log(x2)"
fml |> filter_terms(drop = "log(x2):x1", response = FALSE)
#> ~1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2))
#> attr(,"factors")
#>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2)
#> x1          1       0          0
#> log(x2)     0       1          0
#> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 1 1 1
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: 0x5f32d1b3d848>

# Signatures and order-invariant label matching
make_signature(c("log(x2):x1", "x1 + x2"))
#> [1] "log(x2):x1" NA          
match_labels(c("x1", "log(x2):x1", "I(x2 * x1)"), fml, nomatch = "pass")
#> [1] "x1"         "x1:log(x2)" NA
